newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt group to build $102 mln beet sugar plant.
newsitem.headline: Egypt group to build $102 mln beet sugar plant.

text.p: An Egyptian joint venture will set up a 350 million pound ($102.9 million) beet sugar plant and one of its shareholders said on Wednesday international bidders would be invited shortly to build the factory.

"An international tender could be issued in the next two or three months to build the plant," Mohamed Amin, media adviser to the chairman of Sugar and Integrated Industries (SII) company, told Reuters. "Up until now it is on a turn-key basis."

National Bank of Egypt, Bank of Alexandria, Banque du Caire and Banque Misr are among the state banks which agreed this month with private banks, firms and businessmen to set up the Fayoum Sugar Company with a paid-up capital of 200 million pounds, Amin said.
Its planned output is 120,000 tonnes a year.

Analysts have estimated Egypt's annual sugar demand at 1.79 million tonnes in 1995/96, up from 1.74 million tonnes in 1994/95. Amin said Egypt's consumption last year was estimated at 1.6 million tonnes.

Egypt's production of cane sugar during the 1996/97 production season should reach 1.009 million tonnes in white value terms, 10,000 tonnes lower than in the previous crop year, German statistician F.O. Licht said in a report.
Amin put Egypt's total beet and cane output at some 1.2 million tonnes in the last production season.
Egypt regularly imports some 600,000 tonnes of sugar a year.

The Egyptian government was keen to expand beet sugar production to augment the country's supply of sugar, Licht said. There are two beet processing factories operating in Egypt and a third is expected to start production next season.
One of the factories is currently doubling capacity to 240,000 tonnes a year.
The planned factory, the fourth, will be built in the province of Fayoum, some 100 km (60 miles) southwest of Cairo.
"We (SII)are confident to win the tender because our price is normally 40-60 percent lower than world prices," Amin said.
"We are able to provide at least 84 percent of the plant as we have already the experience of building sugar plants."
The state-owned SII has set up five cane and beet sugar plants in Egypt, and is equipping five others in Iran, he added.

"SIIhas just refitted its Abu Qurqas factory in south Egypt so it can process cane and beet sugar respectively,"Amin said. "If SIIis selected as the winner bidder, the (Fayoum) factory would be ready for production after some two years." $1 = 3.4
